findings.title: Crossed bounds (xl > xu or rl > ru) are reported .optimal at an infeasible point, even after presolve has diagnosed infeasibility
findings.claim: README 2.2: CompiledLP is 'min or max of cᵀx + c0 with rl ≤ Ax ≤ ru and xl ≤ x ≤ xu'; README 2.5: Simplex returns a ray when the answer is .infeasible; Simplex.swift:156-157 comment: 'The unpresolved problem gives one [certificate], and settles the status'; README 3 Risk 1: read the status before the values.
findings.observed: CompiledLP(a: 0x1, c: [1], xl: [2], xu: [1]) -> Simplex(.dual) and Simplex(.primal), with and without presolve: status optimal, x = [2], objective 2, maxViolation bounds 1.0, warning 'presolve found the model infeasible (column x1 has lower bound 2.0 above upper bound 1.0); solving without presolve for the certificate'. One row with rl = 3 > ru = 1 over x, y in [0, 5]: optimal x = [3, 0], row violation 2.0. Same through WarmStart.incremental with BoundChange(column 0, lower 2.5, upper 1.5), CompiledLP.withColumnBounds, SimplexEngine.applyBoundChanges and Automatic(). All 40 configurations of the probe grid answer optimal on four such cases. InteriorPoint answers infeasibleOrUnbounded.
findings.whyWrong: The problem has no feasible point; .optimal with a point that violates its bounds by 1.0 is a wrong answer with a success status. Presolve detected the infeasibility and the final status overrides it.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPSimplex/SimplexEngine.swift:664-677 (primalInfeasibility measures basic variables only; a nonbasic column placed at a crossed bound by placeNonbasic, SimplexEngine.swift:382-389, is never measured); Sources/ZTronLPSimplex/Simplex.swift:155-161 (presolve's .infeasible verdict is replaced by the unpresolved engine run)

findings.title: Primal simplex declares a feasible LP with condition number 1.5e9 infeasible, without a warning and with a dual ray that does not certify
findings.claim: README 3 Risk 1: 'up to a condition number of about 1e10 the solution is recovered'; README 4 defect 8 (fixed): the simplex 'takes a small pivot before it concludes "infeasible"'; HANDBOOK decision 18; README 2.5: a ray when the answer is .infeasible; HANDBOOK Testing: every infeasible result's dual ray is checked numerically.
findings.observed: Instance k15 of a random L·D·U equality family (n = 11, D spans 1e-7, κ₁ = 1.50e9, rows rl = ru = A·1, columns in [-10, 10]). x = 1 satisfies every row exactly in floating point (maxViolation 0); a dense solve recovers x to 2.2e-8. Simplex(.primal) default: infeasible, warnings [], Farkas margin of its dualRay -1.89e-7, which is negative, so the ray certifies nothing. The same holds in all 22 primal configurations of the grid (dense and QR, presolve on and off, scaling none and geometric, Dantzig, steepest-edge and partial pricing, perturbation off and always). InteriorPoint(), whose crossover runs the simplex, also answers infeasible. Simplex(.dual) and Automatic() answer optimal, 2.1e-8 from x = 1. Across the family: 19 more false .infeasible at κ 1e10-1e12 and 22 at κ 1e12-1e14.
findings.whyWrong: The LP is feasible, so .infeasible is a false conclusive verdict. It comes with no warning, at a condition number the README calls safe, and its certificate fails the independent check.

findings.title: After a failed refinement pass, .optimal stands although the refactorized vertex violates feasibility by up to 8e3; the same badly scaled inputs also get false .infeasible verdicts
findings.claim: README 4 Results limit: 'Optimal' means 'feasible and dual feasible to 1e-7'; doc comment of SimplexEngine.refine and HANDBOOK 16: 'The pass can only replace an optimal answer by a better one'; the engine's own warning: 'the solution is optimal within the tolerances'.
findings.observed: KKT-constructed LP (seed 1273, 7x10, |a| in [2.2e-8, 1.0e6]) with Simplex(.primal, factorization: .sparseQR, scaling: .none): optimal, objective 3.94e7 against the constructed -3.07e8 (relative error 1.13), row violation 496, warning 'the solution is optimal within the tolerances, but a violation of 8186.179927012323 remains that pivoting at tighter tolerances could not remove: the problem is ill-conditioned'. The sweep at row and column scales of 10^±4 gave 27 .optimal answers whose own warning reports a violation above 1e-6, and 9 false .infeasible verdicts whose rays have negative Farkas margins and carry no warning. All of these use scaling: .none; the default geometric scaling is right on every instance, and spreads up to 10^±3 are clean in every configuration.
findings.whyWrong: On a fresh factorization the engine measured a violation 8e10 times its tolerance and still returned the status that promises feasibility to 1e-7. refine() restores the basis from before the pass and treats it as optimal, although that re-measurement showed it is not, and the warning text misstates it.

findings.title: 'Beyond a condition number of about 1e11 only the objective can be trusted' holds only for the Hilbert family's objective
findings.claim: README 3 Risk 1: 'up to a condition number of about 1e10 the solution is recovered, beyond it only the objective is (defect 9)'; README 4 defect 9 title: 'Beyond a condition number of about 1e11 only the objective can be trusted'.
findings.observed: Random L·D·U equality LPs (x = 1 unique, generic objective c = Aᵀ1 + 1, 24 instances x 40 configurations). At κ₁ 1e10-1e12 the objective is right (worst 8.1e-8). At κ₁ 1e12-1e14, 165 of 167 .optimal answers have the objective off by more than 1e-6 (worst 1.85 relative); above 1e14, 244 of 244 (worst 3.43). All carry the ill-conditioning warning. In the Hilbert family c = H·1, so cᵀx = 1ᵀHx is pinned by the rows and the objective is right whatever point is returned; that is why the README's measurements look good.
findings.whyWrong: The general statement tells users to trust the objective of an ill-conditioned answer. With a generic objective it is as wrong as the point.

findings.title: No simplex test checks returned duals or reduced costs beyond one textbook LP, and no test covers crossed bounds
findings.claim: README 4 Results limit: 'feasible and dual feasible to 1e-7'; the sign convention in Analysis.swift (dual = sensitivity of the reported objective, logical reduced cost = dual); HANDBOOK Testing: oracle 1, constructed optima.
findings.observed: ConstructedInstance.dual is used only by ZTronLPCoreTests/ScalingTests and ZTronLPTestSupportTests/FixtureTests. SimplexConstructedOptimaTests, ConstructedOptimaCorpusTests, NetlibCorpusTests and IllConditionedTests assert status, objective and primal feasibility only. The one dual check is SimplexBasicsTests.textbookProblem, a single 2x3 maximisation. A wrong dual sign or dual-infeasible reduced costs would pass the suite. My probes found the duals right: 20800 KKT solves, dual-sign violation at most 8.8e-14. IllConditionedTests asserts a distance of at most 2e-5 for a README claim of 'about 1e-6', and no test exercises crossed bounds (A2-01).
findings.whyWrong: Half of the 'optimal' contract, dual feasibility and complementary slackness, has no test that could fail.
findings.evidence: grep: instance.dual only in Tests/ZTronLPCoreTests/ScalingTests.swift:164-173 and Tests/ZTronLPTestSupportTests/FixtureTests.swift:45; analysis.dual! only in SimplexBasicsTests.textbookProblem

summary: Cycle A, F2 (Simplex engine and numerics), claims first. On well-posed inputs the claims held: about 75,000 probe solves found no error in the 52-configuration grid on KKT-constructed LPs (objective, primal feasibility, dual signs, complementary slackness, sign conventions, maximize), on Farkas and recession certificates, on netlib (worst 1.33e-11), on the README Hilbert table, warm starts, limits, degeneracy or the LAPACK/BLAS blocks. There are two critical findings. A2-01: an LP with crossed bounds (xl > xu or rl > ru, reachable through the public CompiledLP initializer and derivations, WarmStart.incremental and SimplexEngine.applyBoundChanges) is answered .optimal at a point that violates its bounds by 1.0, even after presolve has said it is infeasible. A2-02: the primal simplex calls a feasible 11x11 LP with κ₁ = 1.5e9 infeasible, with no warning and a ray that fails the Farkas check. There are two medium ones. A2-03: refine() keeps .optimal when its own re-measurement shows a violation 8e10 times the tolerance; this needs scaling .none on 10^±4 data, which also gives false .infeasible verdicts. A2-04: 'beyond κ ≈ 1e11 only the objective can be trusted' fails for non-Hilbert objectives. Three are low: a README 5 warning count, the SparseQRBasis density doc comment, and no test checking duals or crossed bounds. Probe sources are in verification/probes/cycle-A/Slots/F2, and the log is in verification/cycle-A/F2-simplex.md.
